{"statement": {"value": "-- 90-day vs 180-day active customer compare
-- Author: Sarah Chen — how many lapsed in the last 90?

WITH as_of AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS t
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
)
SELECT
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(DAY, -90, a.t)
      THEN o.customer_id
    END
  ) AS active_90d,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(DAY, -180, a.t)
      THEN o.customer_id
    END
  ) AS active_180d,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN DATEADD(DAY, -180, a.t) AND DATEADD(DAY, -90, a.t)
      THEN o.customer_id
    END
  ) AS active_90_to_180_only
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
CROSS JOIN as_of AS a
WHERE
  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1721383709212, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1723370909212, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "active_customers_90d/04-last_180_compare", "description": "How many customers placed an order in the last 90 days?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- AOV by month from raw orders
-- Author: Sarah Chen

SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  SUM(orders.order_total) / COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS aov,
  COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS order_count,
  SUM(orders.order_total) AS gmv
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
WHERE
  orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1744103876778, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1744276676778, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "aov_monthly/01-canonical_raw", "description": "What is the Average Order Value (AOV) by month?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly AOV via the mart
-- Author: James Wilson — straight off order_details for the PowerBI feed.
-- Grain is line-item, so dedupe via the order header.

WITH hdr AS (
  SELECT
    order_details.order_id,
    MAX(order_details.order_date) AS order_date,
    MAX(order_details.order_total) AS order_total,
    MAX(order_details.order_status) AS order_status
  FROM order_entry_db.analytics.order_details
  GROUP BY
    order_details.order_id
)
SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(hdr.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  AVG(hdr.order_total) AS aov,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count
FROM hdr AS hdr
WHERE
  hdr.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(hdr.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1735427578174, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1735513978174, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "name": "aov_monthly/02-mart_version", "description": "What is the Average Order Value (AOV) by month?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- AOV by month — line-item-level avg (anti)
-- Author: Karen Okonkwo
--
-- !! warning from sarah: this AVG is over order_details rows which is line-item
-- grain, so big orders get over-weighted. Result will diverge from the official
-- monthly AOV. Keeping it because the PRD asked for "avg per row" specifically
-- but the right shape is the canonical_raw version.

SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(order_details.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  AVG(order_details.order_total) AS aov_lineitem_weighted,
  COUNT(*) AS line_item_rows
FROM order_entry_db.analytics.order_details
WHERE
  order_details.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(order_details.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1719292101759, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.kirk@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1719810501759, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.kirk@example.com"}, "name": "aov_monthly/03-weighted_avg_anti", "description": "What is the Average Order Value (AOV) by month?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.kirk@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- AOV by month with prior-year side-by-side
-- Author: Ian Chen — exec deck

WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
    SUM(orders.order_total) / COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS aov,
    COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS order_count
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  cur.order_month,
  cur.aov AS aov_current,
  prv.aov AS aov_prior_year,
  cur.aov - prv.aov AS yoy_delta,
  (
    cur.aov - prv.aov
  ) / NULLIF(prv.aov, 0) * 100 AS yoy_pct
FROM monthly AS cur
LEFT JOIN monthly AS prv
  ON prv.order_month = DATEADD(YEAR, -1, cur.order_month)
ORDER BY
  cur.order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1725128733095, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1726770333095, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}, "name": "aov_monthly/04-with_prior_year_compare", "description": "What is the Average Order Value (AOV) by month?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Avg dispatch lead time by warehouse
-- Author: Ben Porter — operational tile for the ops dashboard

SELECT
  w.warehouse_name,
  COUNT(*) AS line_items,
  AVG(
    CAST(DATEDIFF(DAY, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2)) AS FLOAT)
  ) AS avg_days
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON o.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  w.warehouse_name
ORDER BY
  avg_days
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1719198271690, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1719716671690, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "name": "avg_dispatch_lead_by_warehouse/01-canonical_avg", "description": "What is the average dispatch lead time by warehouse?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Dispatch lead percentiles by warehouse
-- Author: David Kim — the avg is misleading without the tail
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH lead AS (
    SELECT w.warehouse_name,
           DATEDIFF(day, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2)) AS days_to_dispatch
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses  w  ON w.warehouse_id = o.warehouse_id
    WHERE  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
),
pct AS (
    SELECT warehouse_name,
           days_to_dispatch,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_name) AS p50_days,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_name) AS p90_days,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_name) AS p95_days
    FROM   lead
)
SELECT warehouse_name,
       COUNT(*)                                 AS line_items,
       AVG(CAST(days_to_dispatch AS FLOAT))     AS mean_days,
       MAX(p50_days)                            AS p50_days,
       MAX(p90_days)                            AS p90_days,
       MAX(p95_days)                            AS p95_days
FROM   pct
GROUP  BY warehouse_name
ORDER  BY p90_days
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1734117020326, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1734721820326, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "avg_dispatch_lead_by_warehouse/03-with_percentiles", "description": "What is the average dispatch lead time by warehouse?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- CLV distribution
-- Author: David Kim
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH clv AS (
    SELECT customer_id, SUM(order_total) AS lifetime_revenue
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
    WHERE  order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
    GROUP  BY customer_id
),
pct AS (
    SELECT lifetime_revenue,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER () AS p50,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER () AS p75,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER () AS p90,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER () AS p95,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.99) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER () AS p99
    FROM   clv
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*)              AS customers,
    AVG(lifetime_revenue) AS mean_clv,
    MAX(p50)              AS p50,
    MAX(p75)              AS p75,
    MAX(p90)              AS p90,
    MAX(p95)              AS p95,
    MAX(p99)              AS p99,
    MAX(lifetime_revenue) AS max_clv
FROM pct
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1731362683312, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1732053883312, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "clv_distribution_percentiles/01-canonical_percentile_cont", "description": "What does the CLV distribution look like (percentiles)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- CLV percentiles within each customer class
-- Author: David Kim
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH clv AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_class, SUM(o.order_total) AS lifetime_revenue
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders    o
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
    GROUP  BY c.customer_id, c.customer_class
),
pct AS (
    SELECT customer_class,
           lifetime_revenue,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_class) AS p50,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY lifetime_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_class) AS p90
    FROM   clv
)
SELECT customer_class,
       COUNT(*)              AS customers,
       MAX(p50)              AS p50,
       MAX(p90)              AS p90,
       MAX(lifetime_revenue) AS max_clv
FROM   pct
GROUP  BY customer_class
ORDER  BY p90 DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1741723085555, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1741723085555, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "clv_distribution_percentiles/02-with_class_segmentation", "description": "What does the CLV distribution look like (percentiles)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- What share of revenue do the top-decile (top 10%) customers contribute?
-- Author: David Kim — for the 80/20 deck

WITH clv AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    SUM(orders.order_total) AS lifetime_revenue,
    NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY SUM(orders.order_total) DESC) AS decile
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    orders.customer_id
)
SELECT
  clv.decile,
  COUNT(*) AS customers,
  SUM(clv.lifetime_revenue) AS revenue_in_decile,
  SUM(clv.lifetime_revenue) * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(clv.lifetime_revenue)) OVER () AS pct_of_total_revenue
FROM clv AS clv
GROUP BY
  clv.decile
ORDER BY
  decile
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1740270198521, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1740702198521, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "clv_distribution_percentiles/03-top_decile_breakdown", "description": "What does the CLV distribution look like (percentiles)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Cohort retention — first-order month × months-since-first-order
-- Author: David Kim
-- Cohort = customers who placed their first order in a given month.
-- Cell = how many of those customers ordered again in month_offset N.

WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    MIN(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS first_order_at
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    orders.customer_id
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    fo.customer_id,
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at) AS cohort_month,
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS active_month,
    DATEDIFF(
      MONTH,
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at),
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2))
    ) AS month_offset
  FROM first_order AS fo
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON o.customer_id = fo.customer_id AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
)
SELECT
  CAST(labelled.cohort_month AS DATE) AS cohort_month_d,
  labelled.month_offset,
  COUNT(DISTINCT labelled.customer_id) AS active_customers
FROM labelled AS labelled
GROUP BY
  CAST(labelled.cohort_month AS DATE),
  labelled.month_offset
ORDER BY
  cohort_month_d,
  month_offset
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1738524708161, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1739388708161, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "customer_cohort_retention/01-canonical_cohort_grid", "description": "What is monthly cohort retention (% of customers from cohort still ordering N months later)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Just months 0..6 of the retention grid — for the slide
-- Author: David Kim

WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    MIN(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS first_order_at
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    orders.customer_id
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    fo.customer_id,
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at) AS cohort_month,
    DATEDIFF(
      MONTH,
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at),
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2))
    ) AS month_offset
  FROM first_order AS fo
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON o.customer_id = fo.customer_id AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
)
SELECT
  CAST(labelled.cohort_month AS DATE) AS cohort_month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 0 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m0,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 1 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m1,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 2 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m2,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 3 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m3,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 4 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m4,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 5 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m5,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN labelled.month_offset = 6 THEN labelled.customer_id END) AS m6
FROM labelled AS labelled
GROUP BY
  CAST(labelled.cohort_month AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  cohort_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1726429491945, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1726947891945, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "customer_cohort_retention/02-six_month_horizon", "description": "What is monthly cohort retention (% of customers from cohort still ordering N months later)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Retention grid as percentages (vs the cohort size at m0)
-- Author: David Kim

WITH first_order AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    MIN(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS first_order_at
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    orders.customer_id
), labelled AS (
  SELECT
    fo.customer_id,
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at) AS cohort_month,
    DATEDIFF(
      MONTH,
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, fo.first_order_at),
      DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2))
    ) AS month_offset
  FROM first_order AS fo
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON o.customer_id = fo.customer_id AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
), grid AS (
  SELECT
    labelled.cohort_month,
    labelled.month_offset,
    COUNT(DISTINCT labelled.customer_id) AS active_customers
  FROM labelled AS labelled
  GROUP BY
    labelled.cohort_month,
    labelled.month_offset
), cohort_size AS (
  SELECT
    grid.cohort_month,
    grid.active_customers AS cohort_size
  FROM grid AS grid
  WHERE
    grid.month_offset = 0
)
SELECT
  CAST(g.cohort_month AS DATE) AS cohort_month,
  g.month_offset,
  g.active_customers,
  g.active_customers * 100.0 / cs.cohort_size AS retention_pct
FROM grid AS g
JOIN cohort_size AS cs
  ON g.cohort_month = cs.cohort_month
ORDER BY
  g.cohort_month,
  g.month_offset
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1745974968743, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1746838968743, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "customer_cohort_retention/03-with_pct", "description": "What is monthly cohort retention (% of customers from cohort still ordering N months later)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Customers by class

SELECT
  customers.customer_class,
  COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.customers
GROUP BY
  customers.customer_class

{"statement": {"value": "-- Class counts, active customers only (ordered in last 90d)

-- SQL Server can't aggregate over a subquery, so the latest order date is computed once up front.

    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders

{"statement": {"value": "-- Daily counts with DoD % change — flag drops >30%

WITH daily AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) AS DATE) AS day,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(
      DAY,
      -14,
      (
        SELECT
          MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS _col_0
        FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
      )
    )
  GROUP BY
    CAST(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  daily.day,
  daily.orders,
  LAG(daily.orders) OVER (ORDER BY daily.day) AS prior_day,
  (
    daily.orders - LAG(daily.orders) OVER (ORDER BY daily.day)
  ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(daily.orders) OVER (ORDER BY daily.day), 0) AS dod_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN (
      daily.orders - LAG(daily.orders) OVER (ORDER BY daily.day)
    ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(LAG(daily.orders) OVER (ORDER BY daily.day), 0) < -30
    THEN 'alert'
    ELSE 'ok'
  END AS status
FROM daily AS daily
ORDER BY
  day DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Daily orders w/ running 30-day total
-- Author: James Wilson — for the Looker dashboard tooltip

WITH daily AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) AS DATE) AS order_day,
    COUNT(*) AS order_count,
    SUM(orders.order_total) AS revenue
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(
      DAY,
      -30,
      (
        SELECT
          MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS _col_0
        FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
      )
    )
  GROUP BY
    CAST(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  daily.order_day,
  daily.order_count,
  daily.revenue,
  SUM(daily.order_count) OVER (ORDER BY daily.order_day ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_orders,
  SUM(daily.revenue) OVER (ORDER BY daily.order_day ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS running_revenue
FROM daily AS daily
ORDER BY
  order_day

{"statement": {"value": "-- Discount rate by promotion = avg((list - unit) / list) on promoted lines
-- Author: Sarah Chen

SELECT
  pr.promotion_id,
  pr.promotion_name,
  AVG((
    p.list_price - oi.unit_price
  ) / NULLIF(p.list_price, 0) * 100) AS avg_discount_pct,
  SUM((
    p.list_price - oi.unit_price
  ) * oi.quantity) AS total_discount_value
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS pr
  ON o.promotion_id = pr.promotion_id
WHERE
  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  pr.promotion_id,
  pr.promotion_name
ORDER BY
  avg_discount_pct DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- In-transit time distribution
-- Author: David Kim
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

with t as (
    select DATEDIFF(day, CAST(dispatch_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(estimated_delivery AS DATETIME2)) as transit_days
    from   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items
    where  dispatch_date is not null and estimated_delivery is not null
),
pct as (
    select transit_days,
           percentile_cont(0.5)  within group (order by transit_days) over () as p50_days,
           percentile_cont(0.9)  within group (order by transit_days) over () as p90_days,
           percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by transit_days) over () as p95_days
    from   t
)
select avg(cast(transit_days as float)) as mean_days,
       max(p50_days)                     as p50_days,
       max(p90_days)                     as p90_days,
       max(p95_days)                     as p95_days,
       max(transit_days)                 as max_days
from   pct
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1724462568683, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1725153768683, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "dispatch_to_delivery_lead_time/02-with_percentiles", "description": "How long from dispatch to estimated delivery on average?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- In-transit time by delivery type
-- Author: Sarah Chen — confirming "Overnight" actually beats "Express"
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH transit AS (
    SELECT o.delivery_type,
           DATEDIFF(day, CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.estimated_delivery AS DATETIME2)) AS transit_days
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL AND oi.estimated_delivery IS NOT NULL
),
pct AS (
    SELECT delivery_type,
           transit_days,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY transit_days) OVER (PARTITION BY delivery_type) AS median_days
    FROM   transit
)
SELECT delivery_type,
       COUNT(*)                          AS items,
       AVG(CAST(transit_days AS FLOAT))  AS avg_days,
       MAX(median_days)                  AS median_days
FROM   pct
GROUP  BY delivery_type
ORDER  BY avg_days
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1738630612602, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1740445012602, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "dispatch_to_delivery_lead_time/03-by_delivery_type", "description": "How long from dispatch to estimated delivery on average?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly fill rate (% of items dispatched)

  COUNT(*) AS items_ordered,
  COUNT(oi.dispatch_date) AS items_dispatched,

WHERE

  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly GMV — last 12 months
-- Author: Sarah Chen (Senior Data Analyst)
-- Source: orders (raw). For the same number off the mart, see 02-mart_shortcut.sql.
--
-- GMV = SUM(order_total) on completed orders. Per Key Metrics Reference doc,
-- this is "gross" — does NOT subtract returns. See net_revenue_monthly intent
-- for the net version.
--
-- order_status note: shows up as NUMBER(0..4) in raw, mapping not in the docs.
-- 3 and 4 are the two least-frequent in shipped reports, treating those as
-- {On Hold, Cancelled} for the exclusion until finance confirms.

WITH window_bounds AS (
  /* Anchor the 12-month window on the latest order we have. */
  /* Avoids burning the query when the daily feed is late. */
  SELECT
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2))) AS window_end,
    DATEADD(MONTH, -11, DATETRUNC(MONTH, MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)))) AS window_start
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
)
SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count,
  SUM(o.order_total) AS gmv,
  SUM(o.order_total) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS aov
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
CROSS JOIN window_bounds AS w
WHERE
  CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= w.window_start
  AND CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) < DATEADD(MONTH, 1, w.window_end)
  AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4) /* TODO: confirm numeric→status mapping w/ finance */
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1746904574225, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1747206000000, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "gmv_monthly_trend/01-canonical_raw", "description": "What is our monthly GMV over the last 12 months?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly GMV — last 12 months (mart version)
-- Author: James Wilson (BI Developer)
--
-- Hits the analytics.order_details denormalized view to avoid joining 5 tables.
-- order_details is line-item grain — need COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) for order counts
-- and SUM(DISTINCT order_total)... actually no — order_total repeats per line so
-- can't SUM(DISTINCT). Pull a deduped order header CTE instead.

WITH orders_dedup AS (
  /* one row per order with its total + status */
  SELECT
    order_details.order_id,
    MAX(order_details.order_date) AS order_date,
    MAX(order_details.order_total) AS order_total,
    MAX(order_details.order_status) AS order_status
  FROM order_entry_db.analytics.order_details
  GROUP BY
    order_details.order_id
), window_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    DATETRUNC(MONTH, MAX(CAST(orders_dedup.order_date AS DATETIME2))) AS window_end,
    DATEADD(MONTH, -11, DATETRUNC(MONTH, MAX(CAST(orders_dedup.order_date AS DATETIME2)))) AS window_start
  FROM orders_dedup AS orders_dedup
)
SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  COUNT(*) AS order_count,
  SUM(o.order_total) AS gmv,
  AVG(o.order_total) AS aov
FROM orders_dedup AS o
JOIN window_bounds AS w
  ON CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= w.window_start
  AND CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) < DATEADD(MONTH, 1, w.window_end)
WHERE
  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1738237645338, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1738842445338, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "name": "gmv_monthly_trend/02-mart_shortcut", "description": "What is our monthly GMV over the last 12 months?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly GMV with prior-year comparison
-- Author: Ian Chen (Director of Data) — adapted for the exec dashboard
--
-- Adds a prior-year column + YoY % so we can show momentum on the monthly slide.
-- Same canonical GMV definition; just a wider shape.

WITH monthly_gmv AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
    SUM(orders.order_total) AS gmv
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
), window_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    MAX(monthly_gmv.order_month) AS latest_month,
    DATEADD(MONTH, -11, MAX(monthly_gmv.order_month)) AS earliest_in_window,
    DATEADD(YEAR, -1, DATEADD(MONTH, -11, MAX(monthly_gmv.order_month))) AS earliest_prior_year
  FROM monthly_gmv AS monthly_gmv
)
SELECT
  cur.order_month,
  cur.gmv AS gmv_current,
  prv.gmv AS gmv_prior_year,
  cur.gmv - prv.gmv AS yoy_abs_delta,
  (
    cur.gmv - prv.gmv
  ) / NULLIF(prv.gmv, 0) * 100.0 AS yoy_pct_change
FROM monthly_gmv AS cur
JOIN window_bounds AS w
  ON cur.order_month BETWEEN w.earliest_in_window AND w.latest_month
LEFT JOIN monthly_gmv AS prv
  ON prv.order_month = DATEADD(YEAR, -1, cur.order_month)
ORDER BY
  cur.order_month
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1738135573538, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1740381973538, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}, "name": "gmv_monthly_trend/03-with_yoy_compare", "description": "What is our monthly GMV over the last 12 months?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.EMP006"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly revenue trend
-- Author: Karen Okonkwo (Product Manager) — quick check before the prod review
--
-- Note from Sarah: this one drops the order_status exclusion that finance uses
-- for the official GMV. So this number will be higher than the dashboard for
-- months with more cancellations / holds. Still useful as a "top of funnel" view.

{"statement": {"value": "-- Credit limit vs realized spend (top quintile credit limit only)
-- Author: Sarah Chen
-- SQL Server's PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only, so the 80th percentile comes from a one-row TOP 1 lookup.

WITH cust AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, c.cust_first_name, c.cust_last_name, c.credit_limit,
           SUM(o.order_total) AS spend
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.customers c
    LEFT   JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders o
           ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
    GROUP  BY c.customer_id, c.cust_first_name, c.cust_last_name, c.credit_limit
),
p80 AS (
    SELECT TOP 1 PERCENTILE_CONT(0.8) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY credit_limit) OVER () AS credit_limit_p80
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.customers
)
SELECT TOP 25 customer_id, cust_first_name, cust_last_name, credit_limit, COALESCE(spend, 0) AS spend
FROM   cust
CROSS  JOIN p80
WHERE  credit_limit >= p80.credit_limit_p80
ORDER  BY spend DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1725024787888, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1725111187888, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "high_credit_limit_actual_spend/01-canonical_credit_v_spend", "description": "For customers with high credit limits, what is their actual spending pattern?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Credit utilization ratio (spend / credit_limit) — risk/marketing list
-- Author: Sarah Chen

WITH cust_spend AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    c.credit_limit,
    SUM(o.order_total) AS spend
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.customers AS c
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
  WHERE
    o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    c.customer_id,
    c.credit_limit
)
SELECT TOP 25
  cust_spend.customer_id,
  cust_spend.credit_limit,
  cust_spend.spend,
  cust_spend.spend / NULLIF(cust_spend.credit_limit, 0) AS utilization_ratio,
  CASE
    WHEN cust_spend.spend > cust_spend.credit_limit
    THEN 'over_limit'
    WHEN cust_spend.spend > cust_spend.credit_limit * 0.8
    THEN 'high_utilization'
    WHEN cust_spend.spend > cust_spend.credit_limit * 0.5
    THEN 'medium'
    ELSE 'low'
  END AS utilization_band
FROM cust_spend AS cust_spend
ORDER BY
  utilization_ratio DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1741596933743, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1742633733743, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "high_credit_limit_actual_spend/02-with_credit_utilization_ratio", "description": "For customers with high credit limits, what is their actual spending pattern?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Inventory turnover by category — units sold ÷ total on-hand
-- Author: Sarah Chen — over the full data window

WITH sold AS (
  SELECT
    p.category_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY
    p.category_id
), stock AS (
  SELECT
    p.category_id,
    SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) AS total_stock
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON i.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY
    p.category_id
)
SELECT
  c.category_name,
  s.units_sold,
  st.total_stock,
  s.units_sold * 1.0 / NULLIF(st.total_stock, 0) AS turnover_ratio
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories AS c
JOIN sold AS s
  ON c.category_id = s.category_id
JOIN stock AS st
  ON c.category_id = st.category_id
ORDER BY
  turnover_ratio DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1726138026290, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1726656426290, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "inventory_turnover_by_category/01-canonical", "description": "What is inventory turnover by category (units sold / avg stock)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Turnover for last 90 days only, normalised to 90-day-equivalent
-- Author: Sarah Chen

WITH sold_90 AS (
  SELECT
    p.category_id,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(
      DAY,
      -90,
      (
        SELECT
          MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS _col_0
        FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
      )
    )
  GROUP BY
    p.category_id
), stock AS (
  SELECT
    p.category_id,
    SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) AS total_stock
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON i.product_id = p.product_id
  GROUP BY
    p.category_id
)
SELECT
  c.category_name,
  s.units_sold,
  st.total_stock,
  s.units_sold * 1.0 / NULLIF(st.total_stock, 0) AS turnover_90d
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories AS c
JOIN sold_90 AS s
  ON c.category_id = s.category_id
JOIN stock AS st
  ON c.category_id = st.category_id
ORDER BY
  turnover_90d DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1744706822056, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1746262022056, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "inventory_turnover_by_category/02-with_window_period", "description": "What is inventory turnover by category (units sold / avg stock)?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Negative inventory bucketed by severity
-- Author: Julia

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN i.quantity_on_hand BETWEEN -10 AND -1
    THEN 'minor'
    WHEN i.quantity_on_hand BETWEEN -100 AND -11
    THEN 'medium'

{"statement": {"value": "-- Net revenue by month — per the Metrics Reference, sum line-item revenue
-- where return_date IS NULL (i.e. keep only the non-returned value).
-- Author: BID / James

SELECT
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN oi.return_date IS NULL THEN oi.unit_price * oi.quantity ELSE 0 END) AS net_revenue,
  SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS gross_revenue
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE
  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
ORDER BY
  order_month

{"statement": {"value": "-- Net revenue = GMV - returned value (computed as two subqueries)
-- Author: Sarah Chen — keep them separate so finance can audit each line

WITH gmv AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS month,
    SUM(orders.order_total) AS gmv
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
), returned_value AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS month,
    SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS returned_value
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    oi.return_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  g.month,
  g.gmv,
  COALESCE(r.returned_value, 0) AS returned_value,
  g.gmv - COALESCE(r.returned_value, 0) AS net_revenue
FROM gmv AS g
LEFT JOIN returned_value AS r
  ON g.month = r.month
ORDER BY
  g.month

{"statement": {"value": "-- Monthly signups with YoY
-- Author: Ian Chen — exec deck

WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(customers.customer_since AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS signup_month,
    COUNT(*) AS new_customers
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.customers
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(customers.customer_since AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  cur.signup_month,
  cur.new_customers,
  prv.new_customers AS prior_year,
  cur.new_customers - prv.new_customers AS yoy_delta,
  (
    cur.new_customers - prv.new_customers
  ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(prv.new_customers, 0) AS yoy_pct
FROM monthly AS cur
LEFT JOIN monthly AS prv
  ON prv.signup_month = DATEADD(YEAR, -1, cur.signup_month)
ORDER BY
  cur.signup_month

{"statement": {"value": "-- Order → dispatch lead time distribution
-- Author: David Kim — looking at tail risk for the SLA review
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH lead AS (
    SELECT DATEDIFF(day, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2)) AS days_to_dispatch
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
),
pct AS (
    SELECT days_to_dispatch,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER () AS p50_days,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9)  WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER () AS p90_days,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER () AS p95_days
    FROM   lead
)
SELECT
    AVG(CAST(days_to_dispatch AS FLOAT)) AS mean_days,
    MAX(p50_days)                        AS p50_days,
    MAX(p90_days)                        AS p90_days,
    MAX(p95_days)                        AS p95_days,
    MAX(days_to_dispatch)                AS max_days,
    COUNT(*)                             AS line_items
FROM pct
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1729505017277, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1731150217277, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "order_to_dispatch_lead_time/02-with_percentiles", "description": "What is the average time from order date to dispatch?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Lead time broken out by warehouse
-- Author: Sarah Chen — for the warehouse ops review
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH lead_days AS (
    SELECT w.warehouse_name,
           DATEDIFF(day, CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2)) AS days_to_dispatch
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses  w  ON w.warehouse_id = o.warehouse_id
    WHERE  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
),
pct AS (
    SELECT warehouse_name,
           days_to_dispatch,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_dispatch) OVER (PARTITION BY warehouse_name) AS median_days
    FROM   lead_days
)
SELECT warehouse_name,
       COUNT(*)                              AS line_items,
       AVG(CAST(days_to_dispatch AS FLOAT))  AS avg_days,
       MAX(median_days)                      AS median_days
FROM   pct
GROUP  BY warehouse_name
ORDER  BY avg_days DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Products out of stock across all warehouses
-- Author: Ben Porter (Data Engineer) — supports the OOS Slack alert
--
-- "Out of stock everywhere" = SUM(qty_on_hand) over all warehouses is 0.
-- Note: negative quantities can occasionally appear due to CDC race conditions
-- (see the Inventory Staleness runbook). Clamp to 0 so they don't artificially
-- mask a true OOS situation.

SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  p.product_status,
  SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) AS total_stock
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  ON p.product_id = i.product_id
GROUP BY
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  p.product_status
HAVING
  SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) = 0
ORDER BY
  product_name
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1726879150901, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1727311150901, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "name": "out_of_stock_products/01-canonical_having", "description": "Which products are currently out of stock everywhere?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Out-of-stock products with per-warehouse detail
-- Author: Andrea Garcia (Analytics Engineer)
--
-- Same OOS set as the canonical, but expands per-warehouse so ops can see
-- which sites carry the SKU at all. Useful when buyer asks "did warehouse X
-- ever stock this?" — a NULL on the inventories side means never carried.

WITH oos_products AS (
  SELECT
    i.product_id
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  GROUP BY
    i.product_id
  HAVING
    SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) = 0
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name,
  COALESCE(i.quantity_on_hand, 0) AS qty_on_hand,
  i.restock_level,
  CASE
    WHEN i.product_id IS NULL
    THEN 'never carried'
    WHEN i.quantity_on_hand < 0
    THEN 'data anomaly'
    ELSE 'zero stock'
  END AS oos_reason
FROM oos_products AS oos
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON oos.product_id = p.product_id
CROSS JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
LEFT JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id AND i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
ORDER BY
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1731492575499, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1734084575499, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}, "name": "out_of_stock_products/02-with_warehouse_breakdown", "description": "Which products are currently out of stock everywhere?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- OOS products + when they were last ordered
-- Author: Sarah Chen (Senior Data Analyst)
--
-- Merchandising asks for OOS items they can prioritise restocking. Pull the
-- last order date so they can rank by recency of demand: high-demand OOS items
-- restock first.

WITH oos AS (
  SELECT
    inventories.product_id
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories
  GROUP BY
    inventories.product_id
  HAVING
    SUM(GREATEST(inventories.quantity_on_hand, 0)) = 0
), last_order AS (
  /* one row per product with the most recent order date it appeared on */
  SELECT
    oi.product_id,
    MAX(CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS last_ordered_at,
    COUNT(*) AS line_items_lifetime
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY
    oi.product_id
)
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  p.product_status,
  p.list_price,
  lo.last_ordered_at,
  DATEDIFF(
    DAY,
    lo.last_ordered_at,
    (
      SELECT
        MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS _col_0
      FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
    )
  ) AS days_since_last_sale,
  lo.line_items_lifetime
FROM oos AS oos
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON oos.product_id = p.product_id
LEFT JOIN last_order AS lo
  ON oos.product_id = lo.product_id
ORDER BY
  lo.last_ordered_at DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1739213855114, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1741201055114, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "out_of_stock_products/03-with_last_order_date", "description": "Which products are currently out of stock everywhere?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Items overdue (past estimated delivery, never dispatched)
-- Author: Ben Porter

SELECT TOP 100
  order_items.line_item_id,
  order_items.order_id,
  order_items.product_id,
  order_items.estimated_delivery,
  DATEDIFF(
    DAY,
    CAST(order_items.estimated_delivery AS DATETIME2),
    (
      SELECT
        MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS _col_0
      FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
    )

FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items

{"statement": {"value": "-- Overdue items grouped by warehouse — for the daily ops stand-up
-- Author: Ben Porter
-- SQL Server can't aggregate over a subquery, so the latest order date is computed once up front.

WITH latest AS (
    SELECT MAX(CAST(order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS max_order_date
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
)
SELECT w.warehouse_name,
       COUNT(*)                                                                     AS overdue_items,
       AVG(CAST(DATEDIFF(day, CAST(oi.estimated_delivery AS DATETIME2), latest.max_order_date) AS FLOAT)) AS avg_days_overdue
FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi
JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses  w  ON w.warehouse_id = o.warehouse_id
CROSS  JOIN latest
WHERE  CAST(oi.estimated_delivery AS DATETIME2) < latest.max_order_date
  AND  oi.dispatch_date IS NULL
GROUP  BY w.warehouse_name
ORDER  BY overdue_items DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Attachment rate w/ YoY

WITH monthly AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE) AS order_month,
    COUNT(orders.promotion_id) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS attachment_rate
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    CAST(DATETRUNC(MONTH, CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)) AS DATE)
)
SELECT
  cur.order_month,
  cur.attachment_rate AS current_rate,
  prv.attachment_rate AS prior_year_rate,
  cur.attachment_rate - prv.attachment_rate AS yoy_pp_delta
FROM monthly AS cur
LEFT JOIN monthly AS prv
  ON prv.order_month = DATEADD(YEAR, -1, cur.order_month)
ORDER BY
  cur.order_month

{"statement": {"value": "-- Promotion budget vs realised discount value
-- Author: Sarah Chen — per Promo Attribution runbook, budget != actual discount

WITH actual AS (
  SELECT
    o.promotion_id,
    SUM((
      p.list_price - oi.unit_price
    ) * oi.quantity) AS actual_discount
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    o.promotion_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    o.promotion_id
)
SELECT
  pr.promotion_id,
  pr.promotion_name,
  pr.promotion_cost AS allocated_budget,
  a.actual_discount
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS pr
LEFT JOIN actual AS a
  ON pr.promotion_id = a.promotion_id
ORDER BY
  pr.promotion_cost DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1728878192248, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1731128192248, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "promo_budget_vs_actual_discount/01-canonical", "description": "How does each promotion's allocated budget compare to the actual discount given?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Budget vs actual with variance pct (over- vs under-budget)

WITH actual AS (
  SELECT
    o.promotion_id,
    SUM((
      p.list_price - oi.unit_price
    ) * oi.quantity) AS actual_discount
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    o.promotion_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    o.promotion_id
)
SELECT
  pr.promotion_name,
  pr.promotion_cost AS budget,
  COALESCE(a.actual_discount, 0) AS actual,
  COALESCE(a.actual_discount, 0) - pr.promotion_cost AS variance,
  (
    COALESCE(a.actual_discount, 0) - pr.promotion_cost
  ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(pr.promotion_cost, 0) AS variance_pct,
  CASE
    WHEN a.actual_discount > pr.promotion_cost * 1.1
    THEN 'over_budget'
    WHEN a.actual_discount < pr.promotion_cost * 0.5
    THEN 'under_used'
    ELSE 'on_budget'
  END AS status
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS pr
LEFT JOIN actual AS a
  ON pr.promotion_id = a.promotion_id
ORDER BY
  ABS(COALESCE(a.actual_discount, 0) - pr.promotion_cost) DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1741646679263, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1742251479263, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "promo_budget_vs_actual_discount/02-with_variance_pct", "description": "How does each promotion's allocated budget compare to the actual discount given?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Promotional uplift: revenue during window vs equivalent prior window
-- Author: David Kim
-- Promotion windows that have NULL end_date treated as "still running" — skipping those for the comparison.

WITH active_promos AS (
  SELECT
    promotions.promotion_id,
    promotions.promotion_name,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2) AS promo_start,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2) AS promo_end,
    DATEDIFF(
      DAY,
      CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2),
      CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2)
    ) AS promo_len_days
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions
  WHERE
    promotions.promotion_end_date IS NOT NULL
), during AS (
  SELECT
    p.promotion_id,
    SUM(o.order_total) AS revenue_during
  FROM active_promos AS p
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN p.promo_start AND p.promo_end
  GROUP BY
    p.promotion_id
), before AS (
  SELECT
    p.promotion_id,
    SUM(o.order_total) AS revenue_before
  FROM active_promos AS p
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN DATEADD(DAY, -p.promo_len_days, p.promo_start) AND p.promo_start
  GROUP BY
    p.promotion_id
)
SELECT
  p.promotion_id,
  p.promotion_name,
  b.revenue_before,
  d.revenue_during,
  d.revenue_during - b.revenue_before AS uplift,
  (
    d.revenue_during - b.revenue_before
  ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(b.revenue_before, 0) AS uplift_pct
FROM active_promos AS p
LEFT JOIN during AS d
  ON p.promotion_id = d.promotion_id
LEFT JOIN before AS b
  ON p.promotion_id = b.promotion_id
ORDER BY
  uplift DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1720101376550, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1722520576550, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "promo_uplift_baseline_compare/01-canonical_self_join", "description": "How much did revenue lift during each promotion vs the same length window before?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Same uplift but only the % column for the slide
-- Author: David Kim

WITH promos AS (
  SELECT
    promotions.promotion_id,
    promotions.promotion_name,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2) AS ps,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2) AS pe,
    DATEDIFF(
      DAY,
      CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2),
      CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2)
    ) AS length_days
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions
  WHERE
    promotions.promotion_end_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  p.promotion_name,
  (
    SELECT
      SUM(orders.order_total) AS _col_0
    FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
    WHERE
      CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN p.ps AND p.pe
  ) / NULLIF(
    (
      SELECT
        SUM(orders.order_total) AS _col_0
      FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
      WHERE
        CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN DATEADD(DAY, -p.length_days, p.ps) AND p.ps
    ),
    0
  ) - 1 AS uplift_multiplier
FROM promos AS p
ORDER BY
  uplift_multiplier DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1734761940098, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1734934740098, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "promo_uplift_baseline_compare/02-with_pct_lift", "description": "How much did revenue lift during each promotion vs the same length window before?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Uplift only for orders attributed to that promo (more conservative)
-- Author: Sarah Chen — strictly attributed revenue, not all revenue in window

WITH p AS (
  SELECT
    promotions.promotion_id,
    promotions.promotion_name,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2) AS ps,
    CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2) AS pe,
    DATEDIFF(
      DAY,
      CAST(promotions.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2),
      CAST(promotions.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2)
    ) AS length_days
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions
  WHERE
    promotions.promotion_end_date IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  p.promotion_name,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN o.promotion_id = p.promotion_id
      AND CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN p.ps AND p.pe
      THEN o.order_total
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS attributed_revenue_during,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) BETWEEN DATEADD(DAY, -p.length_days, p.ps) AND p.ps
      THEN o.order_total
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS baseline_revenue_before
FROM p AS p
CROSS JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
GROUP BY
  p.promotion_name
ORDER BY
  attributed_revenue_during DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1720899152600, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1722195152600, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "promo_uplift_baseline_compare/03-by_promo", "description": "How much did revenue lift during each promotion vs the same length window before?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Reorder candidates (per (product, warehouse))
-- Author: Ben Porter — feeds the purchase order draft job

SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name,
  i.quantity_on_hand,
  i.restock_level,
  i.restock_level - i.quantity_on_hand AS shortfall
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  i.quantity_on_hand < i.restock_level
ORDER BY
  shortfall DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1741912768228, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1743986368228, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "name": "reorder_candidates/01-canonical", "description": "Show me products that need reordering (qty below restock level)", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Reorder candidates with suggested reorder quantity
-- Author: Ben Porter — for the planner

SELECT
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name,
  i.quantity_on_hand,
  i.restock_level,
  i.reorder_quantity,
  i.max_stock_level,
  LEAST(i.reorder_quantity, i.max_stock_level - i.quantity_on_hand) AS suggested_po_qty
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  i.quantity_on_hand < i.restock_level
ORDER BY
  suggested_po_qty DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1733764995744, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1734110595744, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}, "name": "reorder_candidates/02-with_reorder_qty", "description": "Show me products that need reordering (qty below restock level)", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.bryan@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Reorder candidates, excluding suspected CDC anomalies (qty < 0)
-- Author: Andrea Garcia
-- Per the Inventory Staleness runbook, negative on_hand is a known CDC race condition.
-- Excluding from reorder triggers so we don't double-order.

SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name,
  i.quantity_on_hand,
  i.restock_level,
  i.restock_level - i.quantity_on_hand AS shortfall
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  i.quantity_on_hand >= 0 AND i.quantity_on_hand < i.restock_level
ORDER BY
  shortfall DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1722128776503, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1723424776503, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}, "name": "reorder_candidates/03-exclude_negatives", "description": "Show me products that need reordering (qty below restock level)", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.alex@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Reorder candidates prioritised by shortfall ratio
-- Author: Sarah Chen — ranking which to do first by % below restock

SELECT TOP 50
  p.product_name,
  w.warehouse_name,
  i.quantity_on_hand,
  i.restock_level,
  i.restock_level - i.quantity_on_hand AS units_short,
  (
    i.restock_level - i.quantity_on_hand
  ) * 1.0 / NULLIF(i.restock_level, 0) * 100 AS pct_below_restock,
  i.reorder_quantity
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON i.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  i.quantity_on_hand < i.restock_level AND i.quantity_on_hand >= 0
ORDER BY
  pct_below_restock DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Repeat-order rate using a CTE (easier to extend later)
-- Author: Sarah Chen

WITH customer_orders AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    COUNT(DISTINCT orders.order_id) AS order_ct
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE

), totals AS (

    COUNT(*) AS total_customers,

)
SELECT

FROM totals AS totals

{"statement": {"value": "-- Repeat-order rate via window function on per-order data
-- Author: David Kim
--
-- Window-function take. Slightly heavier than the CTE version but easier to
-- repurpose for "Nth order metrics" later.

WITH ordered AS (
  SELECT
    orders.customer_id,
    orders.order_id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY orders.customer_id
      ORDER BY CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)
    ) AS n
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
  WHERE
    orders.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
)
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT ordered.customer_id) AS total_customers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ordered.n >= 2 THEN ordered.customer_id END) AS repeat_customers,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ordered.n >= 2 THEN ordered.customer_id END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ordered.customer_id), 0) AS repeat_rate_pct
FROM ordered AS ordered

{"statement": {"value": "-- Categories ranked by return rate, plus baseline rate for comparison
-- Author: David Kim

WITH stats AS (
  SELECT
    c.category_name,
    COUNT(*) AS items_dispatched,
    COUNT(oi.return_date) AS items_returned
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p

  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories AS c
    ON p.category_id = c.category_id
  WHERE
    oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    c.category_name
), overall AS (
  SELECT
    SUM(stats.items_returned) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(stats.items_dispatched), 0) AS baseline_rate
  FROM stats AS stats
)
SELECT
  s.category_name,
  s.items_dispatched,
  s.items_returned,
  s.items_returned * 100.0 / NULLIF(s.items_dispatched, 0) AS category_rate,
  o.baseline_rate,
  (
    s.items_returned * 100.0 / NULLIF(s.items_dispatched, 0)
  ) - o.baseline_rate AS rate_vs_baseline,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s.items_returned * 100.0 / NULLIF(s.items_dispatched, 0) DESC) AS rank_by_rate
FROM stats AS s
CROSS JOIN overall AS o
ORDER BY
  rank_by_rate

{"statement": {"value": "-- Return rate within 30 days of dispatch — strict "fast return" window
-- Author: David Kim
-- "Returns within window" is more actionable than lifetime returns because
-- it filters out long-tail returns that may be unrelated to the warehouse.

SELECT
  w.warehouse_name,
  COUNT(*) AS items_dispatched,
  COUNT(
    CASE
      WHEN oi.return_date IS NOT NULL
      AND DATEDIFF(
        DAY,
        CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2),
        CAST(oi.return_date AS DATETIME2)
      ) <= 30
      THEN 1
    END
  ) AS fast_returns,
  COUNT(
    CASE
      WHEN oi.return_date IS NOT NULL
      AND DATEDIFF(
        DAY,
        CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2),
        CAST(oi.return_date AS DATETIME2)
      ) <= 30
      THEN 1
    END
  ) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS fast_return_rate_pct
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
  ON o.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
WHERE
  oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  w.warehouse_name
ORDER BY
  fast_return_rate_pct DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Return rate by channel, with deviation from overall baseline
-- Author: Sarah Chen — for the spotting outliers

WITH stats AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_mode,
    COUNT(*) AS dispatched,
    COUNT(oi.return_date) AS returned
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    o.order_mode
)
SELECT
  stats.order_mode,
  stats.dispatched,
  stats.returned,
  stats.returned * 100.0 / NULLIF(stats.dispatched, 0) AS rate_pct,
  (
    stats.returned * 100.0 / NULLIF(stats.dispatched, 0)
  ) - (
    SUM(stats.returned) OVER () * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(stats.dispatched) OVER (), 0)
  ) AS vs_baseline_pp
FROM stats AS stats
ORDER BY
  rate_pct DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Revenue rolled up to top-level category via the parent_category_id tree
-- Author: David Kim — needed this for the category P&L review.
-- product_categories is self-referential. Recursive CTE to find root for each leaf,
-- then sum revenue under each root.

WITH cat_tree AS (
  SELECT
    product_categories.category_id,
    product_categories.category_name,
    product_categories.parent_category_id,
    product_categories.category_id AS root_id,
    product_categories.category_name AS root_name,
    1 AS depth
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories
  WHERE
    product_categories.parent_category_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    c.category_id,
    c.category_name,
    c.parent_category_id,
    t.root_id,
    t.root_name,
    t.depth + 1 AS _col_5
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories AS c
  JOIN cat_tree AS t
    ON c.parent_category_id = t.category_id
), product_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    p.product_id,
    p.category_id,
    SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS rev
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
    ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
  WHERE
    o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
  GROUP BY
    p.product_id,
    p.category_id
)
SELECT
  t.root_name AS top_level_category,
  SUM(pr.rev) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pr.product_id) AS products,
  MAX(t.depth) AS deepest_subcategory
FROM product_revenue AS pr
JOIN cat_tree AS t
  ON pr.category_id = t.category_id
GROUP BY
  t.root_name
ORDER BY

{"statement": {"value": "-- Channel comparison with AOV
-- Author: Sarah Chen — looking at whether in-store has higher basket size
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH pct AS (
    SELECT order_mode,
           order_total,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY order_total) OVER (PARTITION BY order_mode) AS median_order

)

       SUM(order_total)  AS revenue,
       AVG(order_total)  AS aov,
       MAX(median_order) AS median_order
FROM   pct
GROUP  BY order_mode
ORDER  BY aov DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Total stock value by warehouse — using list_price
-- Author: Ben Porter — for the quarterly inventory carry review

SELECT
  w.warehouse_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT i.product_id) AS sku_count,
  SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) AS total_units,

{"statement": {"value": "-- Stock value using min_price (conservative floor)
-- Author: Andrea Garcia — finance prefers a conservative floor over list price.

  w.warehouse_name,

  SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0)) AS total_units,

{"statement": {"value": "-- Stock value ranking
-- Author: Sarah Chen

WITH wh_value AS (
  SELECT
    w.warehouse_id,
    w.warehouse_name,
    SUM(GREATEST(i.quantity_on_hand, 0) * p.list_price) AS stock_value
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.inventories AS i
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
    ON i.product_id = p.product_id
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.warehouses AS w
    ON i.warehouse_id = w.warehouse_id
  GROUP BY
    w.warehouse_id,
    w.warehouse_name
)
SELECT
  wh_value.warehouse_id,
  wh_value.warehouse_name,
  wh_value.stock_value,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY wh_value.stock_value DESC) AS rank_by_value,
  wh_value.stock_value * 100.0 / SUM(wh_value.stock_value) OVER () AS pct_of_network
FROM wh_value AS wh_value
ORDER BY
  rank_by_value

{"statement": {"value": "-- Time-to-return mean
-- Author: David Kim

SELECT
  AVG(
    CAST(DATEDIFF(
      DAY,
      CAST(order_items.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2),
      CAST(order_items.return_date AS DATETIME2)
    ) AS FLOAT)
  ) AS avg_days_to_return,
  COUNT(*) AS returned_items
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items
WHERE
  order_items.return_date IS NOT NULL AND order_items.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL

{"statement": {"value": "-- Time-to-return distribution
-- Author: David Kim — looking for the "fast return" cliff
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

with t as (
    select DATEDIFF(day, CAST(dispatch_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(return_date AS DATETIME2)) as days_to_return
    from order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items
    where return_date is not null and dispatch_date is not null
),
pct as (
    select days_to_return,
           percentile_cont(0.5)  within group (order by days_to_return) over () as p50,
           percentile_cont(0.25) within group (order by days_to_return) over () as p25,
           percentile_cont(0.75) within group (order by days_to_return) over () as p75,
           percentile_cont(0.95) within group (order by days_to_return) over () as p95
    from t
)
select count(*) as returns,
       avg(cast(days_to_return as float))                as mean_days,
       max(p50)                                           as p50,
       max(p25)                                           as p25,
       max(p75)                                           as p75,
       max(p95)                                           as p95,
       max(days_to_return)                                as max_days,
       count(case when days_to_return <= 7 then 1 end)    as returns_within_7d,
       count(case when days_to_return <= 30 then 1 end)   as returns_within_30d
from pct
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1732410877948, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1732929277948, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "time_to_return_distribution/02-with_percentiles", "description": "How long after dispatch do customers typically return items?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Avg days-to-return by category
-- Author: Sarah Chen
-- SQL Server has no MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT is window-only: compute per row, then MAX per group.

WITH returns AS (
    SELECT c.category_name,
           DATEDIFF(day, CAST(oi.dispatch_date AS DATETIME2), CAST(oi.return_date AS DATETIME2)) AS days_to_return
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items        oi
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.products           p  ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories c  ON c.category_id = p.category_id
    WHERE  oi.return_date IS NOT NULL AND oi.dispatch_date IS NOT NULL
),
pct AS (
    SELECT category_name,
           days_to_return,
           PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY days_to_return) OVER (PARTITION BY category_name) AS median_days
    FROM   returns
)
SELECT category_name,
       COUNT(*)                             AS returns,
       AVG(CAST(days_to_return AS FLOAT))   AS avg_days_to_return,
       MAX(median_days)                     AS median_days
FROM   pct

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top 20 products by revenue — last full quarter
-- Author: Sarah Chen
-- Revenue uses order_items.unit_price (post-discount), NOT products.list_price.

WITH q_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    DATETRUNC(QUARTER, MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2))) AS this_q_start,
    DATEADD(QUARTER, -1, DATETRUNC(QUARTER, MAX(CAST(orders.order_date AS DATETIME2)))) AS last_q_start
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders
)
SELECT TOP 20
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS revenue,
  COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders,
  SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items AS oi
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.products AS p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
CROSS JOIN q_bounds AS q
WHERE
  CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= q.last_q_start
  AND CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) < q.this_q_start
  AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  p.product_id,
  p.product_name
ORDER BY
  revenue DESC

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top revenue products grouped by category for the merch review
-- Author: Sarah Chen — rolls up by category, ranks within

WITH revenue AS (
    SELECT p.product_id,
           p.product_name,
           p.category_id,
           SUM(oi.unit_price * oi.quantity) AS rev
    FROM   order_entry_db.order_entry.order_items oi
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.products    p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.orders      o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE  CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) >= DATEADD(quarter, -1,
               (SELECT MAX(CAST(order_date AS DATETIME2)) FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders))
      AND  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
    GROUP  BY p.product_id, p.product_name, p.category_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT c.category_name,
           r.product_id,
           r.product_name,
           r.rev,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.category_name ORDER BY r.rev DESC) AS rank_in_cat
    FROM   revenue r
    JOIN   order_entry_db.order_entry.product_categories c ON c.category_id = r.category_id
)
SELECT category_name, product_id, product_name, rev, rank_in_cat
FROM   ranked
WHERE  rank_in_cat <= 3            -- top 3 per category
ORDER  BY category_name, rank_in_cat

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top promotions by attributed revenue
-- Author: Sarah Chen (Senior Data Analyst)
--
-- Reference shape from the Promotion Attribution runbook. LEFT JOIN from orders
-- so the same scaffold can be reused for a baseline ("how much revenue is
-- *not* attributed to a promo") without rewriting the join. For this specific
-- question we just filter to promoted rows in the final WHERE.

SELECT TOP 20
  p.promotion_id,
  p.promotion_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_attributed,
  SUM(o.order_total) AS attributed_revenue,
  AVG(o.order_total) AS aov_on_promo,
  SUM(o.order_total) * 100.0 / SUM(SUM(o.order_total)) OVER () AS pct_of_promoted_revenue
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
LEFT JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS p
  ON o.promotion_id = p.promotion_id
WHERE
  o.promotion_id IS NOT NULL /* focus on promoted orders */
  AND o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4) /* exclude held / cancelled */
GROUP BY
  p.promotion_id,
  p.promotion_name
ORDER BY
  attributed_revenue DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1735245890405, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1736628290405, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}, "name": "top_promos_by_revenue/01-canonical_left_join", "description": "Which promotions generated the most revenue?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.sam@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top promos by revenue (promotion-driven join)
-- Author: James Wilson (BI Developer)
--
-- Drives the join from the promotions table, INNER joining orders.
-- Works for this question because we *want* only promoted orders, but the
-- runbook flags this shape as a footgun: if someone reuses it for a baseline
-- ("revenue with vs without promotion") the null-promo orders get dropped.

SELECT TOP 20
  p.promotion_id,
  p.promotion_name,
  COUNT(o.order_id) AS orders_attributed,
  SUM(o.order_total) AS attributed_revenue
FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS p
INNER JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  ON p.promotion_id = o.promotion_id
WHERE
  o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
GROUP BY
  p.promotion_id,
  p.promotion_name
ORDER BY
  attributed_revenue DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1744886671018, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1746269071018, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}, "name": "top_promos_by_revenue/02-inner_join_anti", "description": "Which promotions generated the most revenue?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.jonny2@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top promos by revenue, attributed only within active promo window
-- Author: David Kim (Data Scientist)
--
-- Per the Promo Attribution runbook step 2: enforce that the order_date falls
-- inside [promotion_start_date, promotion_end_date]. Catches data quality
-- issues where promotion_id is set on orders that pre-date or post-date the
-- campaign. Treats NULL end_date as "still active" so we don't drop ongoing
-- campaign attributions.

WITH promo_attribution AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    o.order_total,
    CAST(o.order_date AS DATETIME2) AS order_ts,
    p.promotion_id,
    p.promotion_name,
    CAST(p.promotion_start_date AS DATETIME2) AS promo_start,
    COALESCE(CAST(p.promotion_end_date AS DATETIME2), CAST('9999-12-31' AS DATETIME2)) AS promo_end
  FROM order_entry_db.order_entry.orders AS o
  JOIN order_entry_db.order_entry.promotions AS p
    ON o.promotion_id = p.promotion_id
  WHERE
    o.order_status NOT IN (3, 4)
)
SELECT TOP 20
  promo_attribution.promotion_id,
  promo_attribution.promotion_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT promo_attribution.order_id) AS orders_in_window,
  SUM(promo_attribution.order_total) AS revenue_in_window,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN NOT promo_attribution.order_ts BETWEEN promo_attribution.promo_start AND promo_attribution.promo_end
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS orders_outside_window /* data-quality canary */
FROM promo_attribution AS promo_attribution
WHERE
  promo_attribution.order_ts BETWEEN promo_attribution.promo_start AND promo_attribution.promo_end
GROUP BY
  promo_attribution.promotion_id,
  promo_attribution.promotion_name
ORDER BY
  revenue_in_window DESC
", "language": "SQL"}, "source": "MANUAL", "created": {"time": 1722964328502, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "lastModified": {"time": 1725556328502, "actor": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}, "name": "top_promos_by_revenue/03-with_attribution_window", "description": "Which promotions generated the most revenue?", "origin": "urn:li:corpuser:b2fd91.brock1@example.com"}

{"statement": {"value": "-- Top promos by revenue — mart shortcut

{"statement": {"value": "-- Warehouse throughput via mart
-- Author: James Wilson

WITH hdr AS (
  SELECT
    order_details.order_id,
    MAX(order_details.warehouse_name) AS wh,
    MAX(order_details.order_total) AS total,
    MAX(order_details.order_date) AS dt
  FROM order_entry_db.analytics.order_details
  GROUP BY
    order_details.order_id
)
SELECT
  hdr.wh AS warehouse_name,
  COUNT(*) AS orders,
  SUM(hdr.total) AS revenue
FROM hdr AS hdr
